title: ClientError::InvalidArgument(String) string-typed error path — callers cannot dispatch
description:
src/methods/metadata.rs:76-79, 144-148, 212-215 — three call sites construct ClientError::InvalidArgument(String):

    \"metadata_changes: since_state may not be empty\"
    format!(\"metadata_set: serializing update map failed: {e}\")
    \"metadata_query_changes: since_query_state may not be empty\"

The cause is encoded only in the message string. A caller that wants programmatic dispatch — 'empty-state was caught client-side, retry with a fresh fetch_session' vs 'serialization of an internal PatchObject failed, log and bail' — has to substring-match the message. This is fragile contract leakage:

- 'metadata_changes: since_state may not be empty' is an exhaustively-caught invariant; should be a typed variant the caller can match.
- 'serializing update map failed' wraps a serde_json::Error in a string; the underlying serde_json error type is dropped (no #source chain). A caller cannot do programmatic recovery, only log the message.

Workspace-wide observation: email_set in the canonical sibling (mail-client/src/methods/email.rs:122-126) uses the same shape. So this is propagation of an existing canonical wart, not a regression from canonical. But it freezes a contract that downstream consumers cannot work around.

Suggested fixes:
1. Add typed variants to ClientError (in jmap-base-client) for the empty-state case and the internal-serialization case.
2. Or wrap with #[source] so the serde_json::Error survives via Error::source().

Either fix requires touching jmap-base-client first, then propagating to every *-client crate. Mark as workspace-wide propagation work, but file because the contract decision fossilises at 0.1.0.
close_reason: Triage 2026-10-31 at c07d5206: moot: metadata.rs InvalidArgument call sites deleted in c4496114; crate is pure helpers with no ClientError use (crate-jmap-metadata-client/src/lib.rs:14-36)
